items.text:
The generative marketing machine, as the tools our creative marketers use to
turn a proven ad into finished work for our brands. **Prizm Labs is our
internal system — not for sale.** It is public so the people who work with us
can read every prompt; it is hosted at daemn.co.

Take a video that already worked — a competitor's ad, an organic post,
anything — keep its structure, and rebuild it for one of our brands. You get a
script, a shot list, and a prompt for every frame.

**→ daemn.co** — see it working, with the same ad rebuilt
three different ways. **→ How it works**
— the whole line on one page: swipe, teardown, brief, make, hand-off, live,
performance, and the seven roles that carry it.

   "swap the logo on this picture". Each

Say "pull for updates" and it stays current. Everything is plain text.

**1. Dry run — check everything, spend nothing**

 

Prints OK / MISSING with character counts for: the source, the product, the
brand's variable map, the offer bank, every doctrine slice, every output
format (checked against the element library), each avatar's profile, language
rules and language rows per stage, and — stage by stage — every `{field}` the
prompt names against what the stage is handed, plus the model each stage would
use. No model is called and no file is written. Exits non-zero when something
a run needs is missing. Add `--avatar <key>` to check one avatar instead of
the whole roster.

**2. The run**

 

`--ad` hands in the finished ad the copy runs beside (its story, person, what is
seen and said, its openings): the source stays the proven framework, the ad
supplies the nuance, and stage 8 adds thumbnail lines for its openings.

Files to `runs/copywriter/<brand>/<label>/`: each stage's output, the prompt
as sent, `run.json`, `check.json`. Each stage runs on the model its tier names
(`reads` / `checks` / `designs`); `--tier reads=<model>` repoints a tier,
`--model <model>` forces one model for everything.

After the copy is written (stage 8) the **copy gate** checks it: every price
must be one the brand's offer bank sells today, and no UNFILLED note may be
left in it. A held run keeps everything it made, says why, and does not write
the brief. `--no-gate` skips the gate on purpose.

Then the copy is **read back** (stage 8b) and **checked** (stage 8c). 8b
rewrites eac

h body for the one person reading it: full sentences, one picture
she can see, on this product only, the spice the video scripts get, every
claim and the offer kept word for word. 8c is a reader who never saw 8b's
reasoning: she reads the finished words cold and passes or fails each text. A
fail gets one more 8b with her notes. On the second read, what she passed ships
when at least three texts, a headline and a description survive; otherwise the
run is HELD. The checked copy is written to `final--copy.md`, and that is the
copy every later step reads. Each stage's output is also reviewed by the
creative QC loop (`components/quality-checks`, filed in the run's `qc-log/`);
that review never stops a run.

The avatar's culture map (`brands/<brand>/core-avatars/<avatar>/culture-map.md`)
reaches every writing stage: a straight source stays straight unless the
culture map gives a receipt for a planted joke.

**3. Rerun from a stage — keep what is already written**

 

Every saved stage before the named one is read back, not bought again

items.text:
Three directions, all automatic:

- **Workspace → Drive.** `queue.py ship --auto` (hourly) finds every run in

Clippers, creators, editors and designers all use Prizm Labs from their own

`Shared Assets/handoffs/<role>/<brand>/<your name>/` on Google Drive. Each
hand-off in it carries a `handoff.md` — what this is, who it is for, what is
inside by id, what to do, what must not change, the links, the checks, and

items.doc: How creative marketers work with us — the SOP
items.text:
1. **Get your hand-off folder link.** One Google Drive link from the team.
   A Higgsfield account of your own is enough.
2. **In Higgsfield Supercomputer → Connectors → Explore**, connect **Google
   Drive** and **GitHub**. Sign in to each when asked. (In Claude Code, clone
   the repo and connect Google Drive the same way.)
3. **Put the folder in your own Drive.** Open the link, then in Google
   Drive: right-click the folder → *Organize* → *Add shortcut* → into a
   folder you make in *My Drive*. Supercomputer can only see what is in your
   own Drive.
4. **New chat in Supercomputer → the `+` button → Connectors** — check Google
   Drive and GitHub are both ticked for that chat.
5. **Paste the Day-one prompt** (`prompts/01-day-one-v3-damon.md`) with the
   brand, your role and the folder link filled in. It clones the tools, opens
   your folder and tells you what is waiting. When it ends with *"Set up for
   <brand> — N hand-offs waiting"*, you are done.

items.doc: How creative marketers work with us — the SOP
items.text:
1. **New chat → paste the Pull-briefs prompt** (`prompts/02-pull-briefs-v3-damon.md`)
   with the brand and your role. Name a brief if you have one; otherwise it
   takes the newest hand-off with an empty `returned/`.
2. **It syncs first** — pulls the tools for updates, reads your folder live.
3. **It reads `handoff.md` and lays the brief out**: the scenes with their
   clips and voices (or the image drafts), what must not change, the known
   issues, the loop. Read it. Watch every clip.
4. **Review** — it walks the checklist with you: same person, same wardrobe,
   same product, slop, sound, words, anything odd. You get a table: KEEP /
   FIX AT CUT / REROLL. Then three to five ideas. **You decide** what gets
   rerolled and which ideas to take.
5. **The asks** — the extras the brief wants: scroll stoppers, headlines,
   variations, extra scenes, formats, styles. It makes them in Higgsfield
   from the same cast and product references. You approve each one.
6. **The edit** — for video, the video-edit tool makes the cut itself and
   stops twice for you: the **timeline**, then the **captions**. You approve
   or ask for one change in plain words at each stop. For statics, the
   approved finals go in one folder.
7. **Send it back** — finished files into the hand-off's `returned/`, each
   named `<brief id>_asset-NN`. It walks the checks in `handoff.md` with you.
   The team takes it back from there.

items.doc: How creative marketers work with us — the SOP
items.text:
- **Nothing invented.** Not a product detail, not a claim, not a person. If
  the brief does not say it, the answer is "not in the brief" — ask.
- **Every face and every product carries its reference.** A person or product
  generated without their reference is a reroll, not a delivery.
- **One ratio.** Everything is made and cut at 9:16, with faces, the product
  and every word inside the centred 4:5 crop — the middle 70% of the frame.
  Nothing is made at 4:5 or 1:1. A swipe that arrives 4:5 or 1:1 is rebuilt at
  9:16 the same way.
- **Never write into the hand-off's briefs, assets or references.** Finished
  work goes in `returned/` only.
- **Sync first, every session.** A brief made from yesterday's tools or a
  stale folder is the one that gets sent back.
- **When a door fails — Drive, GitHub, Higgsfield — say which one, in one
  line.** Do not work around it silently.

`--brand` is always named. There is no default brand anywhere in this folder —
a command without one stops and says so, and a run folder whose `run.json`
names no brand is an error that names the file.

`run_month.py` ends `done · N built, M held, K failed · S skipped`; a held email
waits on a ruling and exits 0 — only a failed one exits 1 (HE-2 (held not failed)).

**The dry run is free, and it writes nothing** (2026-09-20). `email.py --dry-run`

model each step would run on, and where the run would file. What only step 0
can know — lane, format, sender — is reported as "decided at triage". The
doctor uses the same dry run and no longer has anything to clean up.

merge tags, typos) under separate headings. Step 2 (`

items.section: `region` — the only thing that makes "nothing else moved" a fact
items.text:
`region` is `left,top,right,bottom` in PERCENT. With it, the shared engine
masks the call (`image_production.providers.edit_in_region`): the picture is
the canvas, the mask exposes that rectangle alone, and the original is pasted
back outside it — so nothing outside can differ, whatever the model did.

Measured on one line of type, 2026-09-22, four live attempts:

what happened.
no region — the product's own label redrew itself every roll ("Centela"→"Centella", "180 g"→"188 g"); held.
region, paste-back only — the label held — and the model had re-composed the frame, so the band carried a SHIFTED copy of the headline; held.
region, masked call, keep-clause prompt — nothing drifted, and the model filled the hole with what was already there — the change never landed.
region, masked call, hole-prompt — nothing drifted; the model painted the band black.
So: a masked edit says what goes IN the hole (`discipline.region_instruction`),
never what to keep — the mask does the keeping. And **type is not a job for a
model**: the `text` fix is deprecated (fixes-v3, 2026-10-07; parked 2026-09-22), agreeing with the standing doctrine (type
is composited over a clean plate, never generated). Wrong words are changed
in the brief's type layer and recomposed — exact, and free.

**Paste a picture ad. Get its structure and a brief for your brand.**

A picture ad is one image, or a carousel (many images you swipe).
This tool looks at the ad. It writes down how the ad is built.
Then it writes a brief: a plan to make the same kind of ad for your brand.

It does not make the picture. A designer, or Image Production, makes it
from the brief.

1. **Higgsfield Supercomputer** or **Claude Code**, with this repo in it.
2. **Your brand folder.** Copy `brands/_TEMPLATE/` to `brands/<your brand>/`.
   Fill it in one time. Say "walk me through it" and it helps you.
   The tool needs three things from it: your **product**, your **customer**
   (who buys), and your **offer** (the price and the deal).

1. Paste the picture ad. (A carousel: paste all the pictures, in order.)
2. Say: **"tear down this picture ad for <your brand>"**.
3. Wait. It works step by step.
4. Read what you get back.

That is all. You do not type commands.

- **The structure.** What is in the ad: the words, the picture, the layout,
  the colors, the order your eye reads it. Nothing about its brand. Just the
  shape.
- **The labels.** What kind of ad it is, from a fixed list.
- **The brief.** The same shape, with your product, your customer and your
  offer inside it. Headlines to choose from. What the picture shows.

- **For the machine (AI)** — the default. A work order for a designer or for
  Image Production.
- **For a creator** — a person with a phone. Say "brief for a creator".
  One simple page: the shot, the words. Nothing technical.

Each step is one prompt in `prompts/`. You can read every one.

Step — What it does.
1 — Looks at the ad and writes down everything in it.
2 — Takes the brand out. Keeps only the shape.
2b — Labels what kind of ad it is.
3 — Puts your brand into the shape.
4 — Writes headlines.
5 — Writes picture ideas.
6 — Writes the brief.
The newest version of each prompt is the one with the highest number
(`-v5-` is newer than `-v4-`).

**Keep the shape. Change the content.** The shape is why the ad worked.
Your product is what changes.

**Nothing made up.** If your brand folder does not say something, the tool
says "I don't know" and stops. That is correct. Go fill in that part of your
brand folder.

- **"missing"** — a file in your brand folder is empty or not there. The
  message says which one. Fill it in.
- **"held"** — the tool checked its own work and found a problem (a wrong
  price, a gap). It says why. Fix that, then ask again.

- `RUN.md` — how to run it by hand, with commands (for people who code).
- `CLAUDE.md` — the full definition.

The query over a brand's customer-language banks: rows in, filtered and ranked
rows out, per stage, provenance travelling on every row. It holds no stage map
and no brand — each chain hands in its own map (see
`tools/video-teardown/machine/language.py`).

Banks live at `brands/<brand>/core-avatars/<avatar>/language/*.json`
(`brands/_TEMPLATE/` shows the shape). Every rendered row carries its id in
[brackets], so a stage can cite what it used. Rows marked `retired` or `burned`
never come back.

`<avatar>/language/used/` holds one file per asset a chain wrote. It is a
record of use, never bank rows — the engine skips it when it loads the bank,
and no bank row is ever edited.

 

`cited` = a stage named the row in its `LANGUAGE USED` block; `matched` = the
words appear verbatim in the brief. `results` is filled from per-ad spend and
purchases joined on the ad name. The video chain's `mark_used.py` (stage 5u)
writes these files; its hooks query asks for unused rows first.

`for_stage(used="fresh")` hands a stage never-used rows first, ranked so the
rows earlier runs were shown least come first (`shown={row id: times}`), plus a
proven slice — up to `proven_share` (a quarter by default) — of rows already
used in an asset. Proven words still work; they stop crowding out the rest, so
runs rotate through the bank instead of every run reading the same top forty.

Rows from a brand's own feedback forms carry `feedback: {stage, areas}`;
`--area <business area>` and `--feedback-stage <stage>` keep only those rows.
With no `AI_WORKSPACE` set, the engine resolves the checkout it sits in —
never a home-folder guess.

Rows can carry the doctrine's awareness level (read in context — who said it,
where, in answer to what), a sophistication signal, the lane their words point
to, `origin` (internal: our own relationship with the customer and any
property where the brand is clearly named; external: everyone else's spaces)
and `voice` (audience or brand-written). `tools/label.py sample|apply` writes
them; `query(awareness=…)` reads them. Identical lines collapse when a query
answers ("said N× in this bank") and the count ranks like likes. A brand's own
accounts go in `brands/<brand>/channels/own-accounts.json`.
`tools/check_names.py --brand <b>` checks row and source ids against the
naming standard.

When you upload a swipe video and ask it to describe every scene, that is a
Gemini model doing the watching.

Use — Model.
First choice — `gemini-3-flash-preview`.
If it is busy — `gemini-3.5-flash`.
For a long or complicated video — `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.

Every still starts here: `text2image_soul_v2`.

Setting — Value — Why.
Size — 1536 × 2048 — portrait, enough resolution to crop.
Style — General — anything else fights your prompt.
`enhance_prompt` — **off** — on, it rewrites you and drifts off the brief.
Seed — fixed, one per character — the same number gives you the same face.
**The character-sheet trick.** Before you generate any scene, make one image
per person as a split-screen sheet: full body on the left, chest-up close-up
on the right, both the same character. Then feed that sheet in as the
reference for every scene they appear in. That is what stops them being a
different human in every shot — it is the single biggest difference between
work that looks made and work that looks broken.

This pack is built from a sweep of nine competitor brands' **live paid ads** —
6,269 ads running right now, spread across 600 different pitches.

You do not need to have run an ad before to use it. Read this page, then the
strategy page, then pick a shape and build.

---

A paid swipe is a collection of ads that companies are **currently paying to
show people**. Not their best posts. Not what went viral. The ads they are
buying space for, today, with money.

items.section: Why that is different from an organic swipe
items.text:
An organic swipe — the videos and posts people share and comment on — tells you
**what people choose to watch**. That is genuinely useful. It tells you what
holds attention, what feels native, what a person will stop for when nothing is
pushing it at them.

A paid swipe tells you something else: **what someone is paying to put in front
of a person who did not ask for it.** That is a harder test, and it is the test
your ads will actually face.

Here is why the difference matters so much.

Ad budgets do not spread out. They concentrate, and they concentrate fast. A
company launches fifteen pitches, two of them make money, and within weeks
almost all of the budget is behind those two. Everything else gets switched off.
Nobody keeps paying to run an ad that loses money — there is no sentiment in it,
and there is no ego in it, because the numbers come in every single day.

So when you look at a brand's live ads and see that one pitch is carrying 835 of
their 1,901 ads, you are not looking at a creative preference. You are looking
at **a survivor**. That pitch beat everything else they tried, and they kept
putting money behind it because it kept paying them back.

That is the whole trick of a paid swipe: **the angles carrying the most ads are
the angles converting.** You do not have to guess which of their ideas worked.
They already spent the money finding out, and the shape of their account tells
you the answer.

One honest limit, stated up front: we can count their ads, not their bank
statement. A big pile of ads on one pitch is strong evidence it is winning, not
proof. The str

**`what-the-spend-says.md`** — the strategy lesson, read straight off these
nine brands' numbers. How hard they concentrate, how many versions they build of
a winner, how much is video versus still images, and what all of that says about
how they sell. Every claim carries its number.

**`angle-shapes/`** — ten files, one per **angle shape** that showed up again
and again across these brands.

An angle shape is **the structure of the pitch, not the subject**. "Hair loss"
is a subject. "Name the two solutions everyone already knows, disqualify both on
a specific cost, then present yours as the third one" is a shape — and a men's
shampoo brand, a testosterone supplement, a skincare brand and a probiotic brand
are all running it right now about four completely different products.

That is why shapes are the useful unit. A subject only helps you if you sell
that thing. A shape works on anything.

Each shape file gives you:

- what the headline does, what the first line does, what the proof is, what the
  close asks for
- a fill-in-the-blank template with `{PLACEHOLDER}` slots
- why it works on a person
- how many ads across how many brands are sitting on it
- a worked example, written out for a made-up brand
- an image prompt and a motion note, so you can make a video version

No brand is named anywhere in this pack. Each one is described by its market
only. No body copy is copied — every template is a rewrite of the structure.

Shape — Ads on it — Brands — What it does, in one line.
`the-spec-sheet` — 1,558 — 6 — Names it flat, ticks off seven facts, asks for the sale.
`the-third-option` — 969 — 5 — Disqualifies the two solutions they already know, offers a third.
`the-two-minute-swap` — 805 — 2 — Not a new routine — replace one item in one they already have.
`the-hidden-culprit` — 534 — 6 — It was never your fault, it was this specific thing.
`the-switch-story` — 408 — 6 — One person, everything they tried, what finally moved.
`the-sorter` — 228 — 2 — You don't have one problem, you have four — here's which.
`the-deadline` — 172 — 7 — A reason today is different from tomorrow.
`the-moment-it-got-noticed` — 160 — 3 — The scene where it stopped being private.
`the-insider-reveal` — 155 — 5 — A study or a professional says the category has it wrong.
`the-somewhere-else-secret` — 123 — 5 — They do it differently over there, and here's why that works.
Those ten account for 5,112 ads. The biggest pitches readable in this sweep
cover 5,260 of the 6,269 live ads — 84% of everything running. The remainder
sits in a long tail of small tests.

Two further shapes recur but sit on too few ads to earn a template; both are
described at the end of `what-the-spend-says.md`.

---

**1. Read `what-the-spend-says.md` once.** It is short. It tells you how much to
concentrate and how many versions to build, and those two decisions matter more
than which shape you pick.

**2. Pick two or three shapes, not ten.** Start with the ones carrying the most
ads across the most brands — `the-spec-sheet`, `the-third-option`,
`the-hidden-culprit`, `the-deadline`. Those four are running in five to seven of
the nine brands. They travel.

**3. Fill the slots from the brand folder.** Every `{PLACEHOLDER}` in a template
is a question about your brand — who the customer is, what they already tried,
what the thing actually does, what the offer is. The brand folder has those
answers already written down. Do not invent them at the keyboard; go get them.
If a slot has no answer in the brand folder, that is a gap worth naming, not a
gap to paper over with a guess.

**4. Hand it to the teardown kit to build.** The shapes here are the *pitch*.
The teardown kit turns a pitch into a shot-ready piece: the hook, the beats, the
on-screen text, the shot list. Each shape file ends with an image prompt and a
motion note written to feed straight into that step.

**5. Build several versions of the one that works.** This is the single biggest
lesson in the numbers, and it is on the strategy page in detail. These brands do
not find a winner and move on. They find a winner and build it another two
hundred times.

lanes:

- **ad**: built only from real customer quotes a brand hands over; the product

Stage — Prompt / code — Makes.
Pack — `pack.py` — the language pack: never-used customer sentences from the brand's language layer, spent phrases removed.
0 Discovery — `prompts/00-discovery-v1-damon.md` — territories: a real-life drama, where her skin collides with it, the exact words to build with and why.

The edit, as small commands. An editor's agent runs them inside **Higgsfield
Supercomputer** (its sandbox already has ffmpeg, Python, Pillow,
faster-whisper and the caption fonts), or on any laptop with Python and
ffmpeg. The editor never types a command: they say "edit this brief" and the
`edit-brief` skill runs these.

One file does the work (`edit.py`), one file holds every number
(`settings.json`), and one file lines captions up with the script's spelling
(`spelling.py`). No brand lives here: a brand arrives only through the brief.

A folder with the brief's clips and a **cut sheet** (`cut.json`), written
from the brief's CUT-SHEET.md. See `example-cut.json`:

 

- **scenes** play in this order, hard cuts only. A talking clip is cut to its
  sound; `keep` names pauses (from `listen`) that stay because they land a beat.
  `talks: false` plays a picture as asked. `still` holds a plate.
- **overlays** are the hook and cards: the exact words and line breaks. `with`
  ties one to a scene (the hook sits on frame one for its whole first scene).
- **line** (optional) gives the script's words, so captions use its spelling.
- **captions.look** picks a look from `settings.json` (`bold-highlight`, `clean-lower`, `one-word`, `word-box` —
  the sung or said word on its own coloured box, for song ads).
- **punches** (optional) are extra 7% push-ins, in seconds on the rough cut's
  clock, put in before any type goes on.

Step — Command — What it does.
Check the machine — `edit.py doctor` — What's installed, which steps can run.
Listen — `edit.py listen scenes/*.mp4` — Per clip: start/end silence, breaths, pauses numbered P1, P2…, a line that runs into the clip's last frame, loudness.
Cut to the sound — `edit.py cut cut.json --out rough.mp4` — Start/end silence out, breaths kept, pauses cut unless kept, 7% punch-in after each cut pause, every clip levelled to −16 LUFS, scenes in order.
Words — `edit.py words rough.mp4 --out words.json --sheet cut.json` — Word timings off the sound, in the script's spelling when lines are given.
Captions + cards — `edit.py captions rough.mp4 words.json --out captioned.mp4 --report rough.report.json` — 2–4 words at a time, the spoken word lit; the hook and cards from the sheet. Type is always a layer on top.
Punch-ins — `edit.py punch in.mp4 --at 3.2-4.1 --out out.mp4` (or `punches` in the sheet) — Extra 7% push-ins on chosen moments, sound untouched.
Frame fixes — `edit.py frame clean in.mp4 out.mp4` (also `seams`, `bridge`, `loopclose`, …) — Runs `../video-edit/frame-control/framectl.py`; needs `pip install numpy 'opencv-python-headless<5'`.

Loudness — `edit.py loudness master.mp4` — Integrated LUFS and true peak.
Master — `edit.py master captioned.mp4 --out master.mp4` — room tone under everything, −14 LUFS, −1 dBTP; picture copied untou

ched.
Final gate — `edit.py check master.mp4 --report rough.report.json` — 9:16 1080×1920, length, never black, mastered, no dead air (0.7 s or more).
All of it — `edit.py run cut.json --out-dir out` — cut → words → captions → master → safe zone → checks, one 9:16 master.

items.section: The rules it carries (the settled edit line)
items.text:
- Silence is heard in the sound (quieter than −35 dB for 0.15 s), never read off the words.
- Start and end silence: always cut, leaving 0.10 s before the first sound and 0.18 s after the last, so a line
  rings out and no syllable is clipped. Breaths (under 0.35 s): always kept.
- Mid-clip pauses (0.35 s or more): the kit proposes cutting them and lists
  them; the editor keeps any that land a beat. A kept pause of 0.7 s or more
  shows in the final gate as dead air, so it is a choice someone made.
- After a cut pause the next piece is 7% closer — it reads like a second camera.
- No piece under half a second (no flashes): a pause that would leave one is kept, and the report says so.
- Every piece's sound fades in and out over 12 ms, so no join clicks.
- Never digital silence: the master carries a quiet room (about −50 dB) under everything, far below what the
  dead-air check listens for.
- A clip whose line runs into its last frame is **cut off**: the cut stops and
  the clip goes back to production. `--anyway` makes a review cut only.
- 9:16 only. Faces, product and every word sit inside the centred 4:5 band
  (the middle 1080×1350 of 1080×1920) and clear of the app's buttons.
- The master is −14 LUFS with peaks at or under −1 dBTP.

The sandbox is wiped seconds after each call, so one call does everything:
fetch the kit, fetch the clips, run, upload the master.

 

Run it with `background: true` (a 60-second piece takes well under the
15-minute lease) and read the log with a second call.

**The model decides, the sheet records, the machine executes, the owner approves.**
The cut sheet (`machine/cutsheet.py`) is the one file that IS the edit. Nothing
else knows what is in the video. A change is a new version of the sheet —
never a regeneration — and every change is kept with its reason.

The engine is HyperFrames (HeyGen, Apache-2.0, installed on this Mac
2026-09-20): a video is a web page with timing marks, rendered frame by frame,
so the same sheet always gives the same video. `machine/compose.py` is the only

items.section: The steps — `machine/steps.json` is the list; the page and the runner both read it
items.text:
gather → cut → gate → **STOP 1 timeline** → **STOP 2 captions** → export →
checks → file → learn.

the owner's order, 2026-09-20: see the timeline with the dead space out; then the
captions on; then the final export. Every change runs back through learning.

- **A talking clip keeps its own sound.** That is the only thing that keeps the
  lips right (the owner, 2026-09-20, on the first proof: "the lip sync is off… the
  A-roll was already good"). A separate voice file laid over a talking clip is
  refused as two voices. The finished file is measured against the source clip
  (`machine/syncheck.py`); more than one frame of slip is HELD.
- **Dead air is cut ON the clip.** Talking A-roll is split at every pause longer
  than the pace dial — picture and sound together, a breath left each side — and
  alternate cuts punch in 7% so a jump reads as a choice. B-roll hides the rest.
- **B-roll over the voice read has no lips**, so its voice slice is cut freely
  and the picture runs on (`voice_cuts`). A piece with no talking clip at all
  may use one whole voice track instead.
- **B-roll is placed by the WORDS it covers**, never by seconds, so it survives
  re-timing (`covers: {"from": "is why", "to": "worked"}`).
- **A headline that opens the video is there on frame one** — no fade, no slide —
  and lives exactly as long as the clip under it (`with: <clip id>`).
- **Nothing unapproved reaches the edit.** `gather` refuses a clip without
  `approved: true`, and a clip with no roll label.
- **A-roll carries the line, B-roll covers it.** B-roll with nothing under it —
  no A-roll and no voice cut — is refused. The roll labels come from the teardown and the brief, not from here.
- **Nothing renders red.** The gate names the field: a hole in the picture, a
  trim past the source, a caption or overlay inside the safe zone, a look or
  transit

ion that is not on its list, a cut with no `why`.
- **Text is a layer, never a generation.** Captions, hooks and the end card are
  composed on top. A caption look is a SETTING (`looks/bank.json`); switching it
  never re-edits the footage. `match-swipe` builds a one-off look from the
  teardown's caption read.
- **The editing rules are checks, not taste:** nothing moves in a straight
  line; never a lone fade; exits twice as fast as entrances; one loud colour per
  frame; no frozen stills; captions 2–4 words, one highlight, inside the safe
  zone; a sound effect lands two frames early; music 18 dB under the voice.
- **The edit only assembles** (the owner, 2026-09-23: the teardown names every element,
  the brief carries it, production makes it, the edit assembles it — "all these
  elements need to be green"). Every element in `tools/video-production/ELEMENTS.md`
  is laid by `machine/assemble.py` and drawn by `compose.py`: card · screen (per surface)
  · split · greenscreen · endcard · lower thirds · annotations · platform UI ·
  disclaimers · transitions · one grade · music · SFX · room tone. A card's, screen's
  or endcard's words must match the plan word for word; a plate, bank file or
  disclaimer that is not there is RED by name (`unmade`), never skipped.
- **Words sit in zones, in named fonts, one space apart** (the owner, 2026-09-23: safe zones,
  fonts, bubble styles, "a lot of space between words", transitions, icons — "everything in
  my repo synced with the same language and components"). Every text layer names a ZONE in
  `looks/placement.json` (never a raw hei

ght): each zone is inside the 4:5 content band and
  clear of every feed's buttons (`defaults.json → safe_zones.surfaces`, the strictest of
  `platform_surfaces`). `machine/placement.py` moves a layer off the face when production
  marks one (`subject_box` per scene) and off words already on screen, and the sheet
  records why; no box = a WARN "face-blind". Fonts are ids in `looks/fonts.json`, LOCAL
  files for a same-every-time render — `machine/fonts.py` lists and (only when run with
  `install`) fetches them; until then the fallback draws and the gate WARNS. Platform UI
  is a style row (`looks/platform_ui.json`); icons, emoji, stickers and drawn elements are
  rows in `looks/icons.json` (`machine/icons.py`, same rule); transitions are a catalogue
  with what triggers each (`looks/transitions.json`). An unknown id is RED.
- **Sound is laid by rule:** music ducked 18 dB under the voice (a volume lane that
  comes up only where nobody speaks) and cut so the last frame lands on a bar of its
  tempo; a sound effect lands two frames early; room tone under every trimmed join
  and silent span; the finished file mastered to −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP. The
  edit does NOT re-check the voice itself — production owns the audio check.
- **Disclaimers come from `brands/<brand>/brand-identity/compliance.json`, read-only**, by claim

items.section: The variation chain — where scale actually comes from (2026-09-02)
items.text:
One approved production feeds unlimited variations. That is the multiplier:
the expensive part (deciding the film, casting it, proving it) is paid once,
and every restyle after it is cheap.

**A variation is not a new film.** Screenplay, blocking, dialogue,
mechanics and edit are frozen; only the rendering swaps. `method-05-format-
variation.md` is the doctrine, written from a real run — including its two
recorded failures, which the chain is shaped to prevent:

- **Re-planning.** Handing approved prompts to a model to "restyle" made it
  re-plan the film — new framing, paraphrased dialogue — and the result read
  as a different film. So **stage v3 is not a model.** `machine/restyle.py`
  does exactly three mechanical things (style lock prepended · media swapped
  · photoreal descriptors stripped) and prints its own diff, so the
  guarantee that every approved word survived is auditable.
- **Re-describing.** Generating a "new base" from a text description
  produced people who were not the approved cast, and a product that was
  not the real product. So v2 converts FROM the refined source — the trained
  identity, the approved plate, the real packshot — and marks any asset with
  no source `⚠ NO SOURCE` rather than inventing one.

**The axis distinction, because it decides which chain runs.** A variation
changes how the film LOOKS. Changing the avatar, the problem or the angle
changes what the film SAYS — that is a new production through stage 0b with
different inputs, not a variation. Both scale; they are not the same lever
and conflating them is how a "variation" quietly

items.text:
- **The Drive carve-out (O9).** The media stayed on Drive at its lab path when
  the code moved into `components/`, so the mirror above still reads as a lab
  path. The standing ruling is that Drive is reached by fileId through the API,
  not by the mounted folder. Migrating is its own card; until it lands, the lab
  path is deliberate, and this file says so rather than leaving it to look like
  an oversight.
- **A records adapter (O12): none yet.** The convention allows "an adapter or
  'none yet' stated"; this states it. Worth knowing for whoever builds one:
  `chain_records.py` is cheap because it did not mint a kind — it files onto an
  existing one and distinguishes itself with a single constant. One shared kind
  behind one adapter is 50–100 lines per component; a kind of its own is
  450–650 plus a manifest plus worker wiring.

**A brief goes in. Finished clips come out — one command, nobody at a keyboard.**

This lane is brand-, provider- and format-agnostic. Nothing in `machine/`,
`prompts/` or `formats/` names a brand, a product, a person or a model — a run
names its brand and its format, and the provider is detected or picked. It is
the twin of `image-production`, which is stage two for statics.

Full detail: `formats/RUN-PROTOCOL.md`.

1. **Teardown classifies and injects** → a baseline brief (`tools/video-teardown`, its own machine).
2. **At stage 5 the route is decided** — creator (a real person) or AI. This protocol reads that decision; it never re-decides it.
3. **Stages 5–8 build the brief** for whichever route was picked.
4. **Creator route** → the brief goes to the person through the Google Sheet system. This machine stops.
5. **AI route** → the AI-lane brief is this machine's intake. Everything below is the AI route.

**Format** — a row in `formats/bank.json`, written from `formats/TEMPLATE.md`.
An unknown format is refused; a new one gets a profile and a row first.
Bank + all seven profiles: `formats/README.md`.

**The door** — not a choice since 2026-09-18: every station is a direct
call on our own keys (the one hand, below). `--provider fal |
higgsfield-mcp | higgsfield-ui` still exists to force a piece into a house
on purpose; nothing uses it by default. The ruling per model and door:
`providers/MODEL-HOUSE.md`; rates, ceilings, request shapes and the history
of every door ruling: `machine/providers.json`.

**Brand** — read, never written. A run's `brand` field points at
`brands/<brand>/`; there is no code to change to add one.

the run names — and the lane reads.
`"brand": "<brand>"` — `brands/<brand>/element-facts.json` — what is true of each product, and which elements are blocked.
`cast.presenter` / `cast.who` / `cast.says` — the prompt shape names nobody; the identity comes from the plan.
`cast.face` / `.room` — the cast sheet and the room reference the stills are seeded from.
`runs/ai-elements/<brand>/casting/<name>/voice.json` — the character's cloned ElevenLabs `voice_id`.
— — Drive `Shared Assets/brands/<brand>/finals/<run>/`.
**To add a brand:** create `brands/<brand>/ai-elements/element-facts.json`, build its
cast (`building-the-cast.md`) with a `voice.json` per character, and point
a run at it. There is no code to change.

items.section: The run — the protocol's gates, in order
items.text:
One command runs the whole protocol (`machine/RUN.md`):

Full detail, including which gates each verb runs: `formats/RUN-PROTOCOL.md`.

# — Gate.
1 — Platform plan shown.
2 — Preflight green.
3 — Generate stills.
4 — QC each still.
5 — Verify each still against its cast sheet.
6 — Motion, only on verified frames.
7 — Motion QC.
8 — Director pass.
9 — Coverage gate.
10 — Receipt.
11 — Naming gate.
12 — Editor pack.
Which door each station uses: `machine/providers.json` (the code's map).
The process: `THE-CHAIN.md` (since 2026-10-03, the owner).
What the gate enforces on each model's inputs: `machine/model-inputs.json`.

**The prompts are files.** `prompts/stage-0-read-brief` … `stage-6-handoff`,
versioned, on the teardown machine's convention. Each carries one fenced
`shape` block that `prompt.py` loads at run time. **Edit the file and every
brief made after it changes** — uniformly, without touching code. They are
rendered verbatim on the board, because a rule nobody can read is a rule
nobody can correct.

Or from the board — `python3 machine/board.py runs/<run>/` (:8456): press
Generate on a card and `machine/drain.py` makes the take on the direct
doors in the background (frame → line → Omni recipe; cutaway → Omni
silent), then the clip appears in the card. Proven live 2026-09-18 from a
two-order queue. `chain.py` (the gates as text), `pull.py` (a take back
from a house), `ship.py` (→ Drive finals) are unchanged in role.
The process is `THE-CHAIN.md` (since 2026-10-03); the per-scene method is `SCENE-GENERATION.md`.

The swipe side runs on Eugene Schwartz's frameworks, held once in
`components/marketing-doctrine/` and pulled into every machine: five
awareness levels (each with a must-not), five sophistication stages, seven
techniques, and the sections as a vocabulary of what each part of a
video is doing. Every swipe gets a doctrine read right after ingestion and
is banked in the framework bank; expansion reaches for a technique only with
a bank row or a research receipt; the spice pass adds the creative layer
with a cast voice cloned then adjusted, rights on file. The brief that
arrives here carries Section · Technique · Emotion · Outcome per scene, and
this machine's scene shapes and mood rules are bound from the same doctrine
(`{techniques}`, `{mood}`). Research fires by wiring: the language-bank
query and the research gatherer (`components/research-gatherer/`) resolve
as stage inputs on every run. Record: `PROMPT-CHANGES.md`.

`runs/video-production/<brand>/<label>/`, per the repo-root `runs/README.md`
(2026-09-17 ruling): `run.json`, `frames.json`, `lines.json`, `batches/`,
`ledger.json`, `deliverable/`. Media never enters git; `.gitignore` enforces
it. The local `M/runs/` and `machine/runs/` folders are media from before that
ruling, both gitignored — not the live destination. The style board and the
pipeline view render to `runs/video-production/_system/` (ignored).

What it is — Live / archive.
`AI-CREATIVE-LINE.md` — the story of the whole line, swipe to motion — live.
`BRIEF-SPEC.md` — the brief shape, ruled 2026-09-14 — live.
`PLATE-CHECK.md` — the plate check — every still judged by measurement before anyone sees it — live.
`building-the-cast.md` — how a character is built, once per person, serves every format — live.
`frames-by-edit.md` — how a frame is made — a reference beats a description — live.
`format-variation.md` — restyling an approved piece into a new visual format — live.
`handoff-and-edit.md` — what the editor receives — live.
`archive/THE-CINEMA-LINE.md` — the coded Higgsfield talking-ad route, proven 2026-09-12/13 — superseded by the Omni door — archive.
`REPO-AND-DRIVE.md` — mirror of the Repo and Drive artifact — live.
`PRINT-RUN-260912.md` — a print record — two finished ads, one torn-down source — live (record).
`chain_config.json` — the 13-stage design; only `machine/pipeline.py` reads it; two stages point at parked prompts — live (design, not the running code).
`formats/` — the bank (`bank.json`), one profile per format, `RUN-PROTOCOL.md` the run, `TEMPLATE.md` — live.
`providers/` — `MODEL-HOUSE.md` (the door ruling per model) + `research/` dossiers + `fal.md` house notes; `higgsfield.md` and `EDITOR-SHEET.md` moved to `archive/` — live.
`prompts/` — one folder per stage, versioned files, current at the top — live.
`prompts/stage-5b-motion-qc/` — the motion QC prompt — gate 7 — live.
`prompts/stage-5c-director/` — the director-pass prompt — gate 8 — live.
`machine/` — the code — `run.py` + the direct doors (`d

irect_openai`, `direct_google`, `voice`, `omni`, `direct_byteplus`), the gates (`platform`, `preflight`, `lineparity`, `deliver`), `providers_fal` for a forced house — live.
`machine/run.py` — the one runner — `start · record · pack` — live.
`machine/omni.py` — the talking beat and silent motion on fal Omni — the controlled recipe as one call — live.
`machine/providers_fal.py` — fal as a forced house, and the queue helpers `omni.py` reuses — live.
`machine/RUN.md` — the runner's own page — authoritative for `run.py` — live.
`ROADMAP.md` — the plan — three legs, in order — live.
`archive/` — history — process, workplan, stages/, sequence-flow, evidence, parked-v1, the Cinema line, the editor sheet, Higgsfield house rules, See `archive/README.md` — archive.
`runs/` — local pre-ruling media, gitignored — archive (superseded).
repo-root `runs/video-production/` — where filed runs land, per `runs/README.md` — now holds the three filed 16 Sep runs — live.

See `ROADMAP.md` — three legs, in order: one command (leg 1, landed), the
print line (leg 2), assembly (leg 3).

**video-teardown** — takes **a video ad**, makes **its element labels and a
brief to remake it**. Does not **produce the video**. Triggered by
`python3 machine/run.py <video> --brand <brand>` (add `--dry-run` to check the
whole plan and spend nothing).

the owner's teardown chain: a swiped video goes in, a shot-ready creator brief
comes out. **Graduated from `the team notes/` 2026-08-25 (the developer ruling); homed at `tools/video-teardown/` same day under the three-station design** — the first lab graduation after PM, run deliberately as the worked example of the
process. `README.md` is the doctrine: it is the owner's, written in his voice,
and his corrections outrank anything a session writes here.

**A LIBRARY — the public surface** (the developer, 2026-10-07, triage action 6 (declare public surfaces), provisionally on the owner's behalf — he sees it in the decision log and may strike any line; this clause replaces TI-1 (adapter card) as the contract callers rely on). Callers put `machine/` on the path or load one file by path, and may use only these names:
1. **Commands:** `machine/run.py <video> --brand <b> [--route --label --creator --product --for-avatar --from --to --only --stages]` (mini: `--source`) — a working run in `machine/runs/<slug>/`, filed to the two shelves below; `machine/swipe_match.py <run> [--approve-structure … | --damon-read]`; `machine/compose.py plan`.
2. **Production's gates** (pure reads of a brief's text): `swipe_match.stamp_of(text)` → `PASSED|HELD|STALE|None`; `swipe_match.read_of(text)` → `APPROVED|STALE|None`; `swipe_match.brief_hash(text)

` → the 16-hex fingerprint; `manifest.status_of(text)` → `COMPLETE|MISSING|STALE|None`; `manifest.check(run_dir, brand, brief_name)` re-checks and rewrites the block; `spoken_check.check_lines([(id, text)])` → `[{id, text, found}]`; `cast_match.check(run_dir)` (findings at `[1]`), `cast_match.readable_mismatches(body, doc, brand)` and `cast_match.scene_mismatches(doc, brand)` → `[{n, element, why}]`; `cast_match.repair(run_dir)`.
3. **Helpers:** `deepen.ask(media, prompt)` → the model's text; `transcript.scribe_only(media)` → `{words: […]}`; `culture.pull(dir, url, runner=)` → `(path|None, why)`; `md.render(markdown)` → HTML; `chain.drive_root()` → the Team Drive `Path` (raises `MountError`); `chain.stages(brand, asset_type, route, lane)` → the stage list, with `chain.route_for`, `chain.PROMPT_HOMES`, `chain.GEMINI_MODEL`, `chain.CLAUDE_MODEL`; `tools/gemini_breakdown.key()`, `.req(url, …)` → parsed reply, `.BASE`; `tools/storage.drive_root()` → `Path|None`.
4. **Read by path:** `machine/runs/<slug>/` (`run.json`, `stages/1-teardown.md`), `records/creators/<handle>/`, `machine/chain_config.json`, and `prompts/` + `README.md` read or copied whole — a reader that pins one prompt version by file name carries its own risk.
5. **SEAM, not public:** `run._clean_env()` (ad-variations `proven_to_format.py`). A seam renamed keeps its old name as an alias until its callers move. `keys.py` is NOT on this surface: four callers import it for keys read by path, a wall; they move with the keys work (video-production#1 (keys by path)).
Everything else in `machine/` and `tools/` is internal
and may change without notice. The tests in `new-workflow-design/builds/vt-multiuser/` and `teardown-integration/` test internals on purpose and are not callers.

1. **the owner owns this folder and this folder is primary.** He works here the
   way he always has — sentences into a Claude session, the session runs the
   CLI (`machine/run.py`), the board is the view. Preserving that experience
   is a ruled design constraint, not a preference.
2. **His notes are his.** `notes/`, TODOs, and wants-next files are the owner's
   own roadmap — never a work queue for anyone else. Work reaches the team
   only when he flags it explicitly (process being designed in PM).
3. **Sessions other than the owner's touch this folder only for**: the
   runs→records adapter surface, path/key graduation mechanics, or a change
   the owner asked for — and anything ambiguous stops and asks him.
4. **Agnostic on every axis — brand, product, avatar — in the prompts AND
   in the code (the owner, 2026-08-25; product + avatar made explicit
   2026-08-30).** Workspace rule 7 applies here with teeth, because this
   machine is meant to run on any piece of content for any brand we own.
   Rework an *example* freely — an example is illustrative and always was,
   and a prompt should say so at the top, before its first example, not
   only in a footnote. But **nothing that gets filled in at run time may
   name a brand, a product, a category or an avatar.** That detail arrives
   only through variables resolved from `brands/<brand>/`. The same test
   applies to code: a word list, a regex, a path or a default that only
   makes sense for one brand is a bug, not a shortcut. If a rule cannot be
   written without naming the brand, it belongs in that brand's folder,

not in this machine.
5. Media and run outputs live on the team Drive, never in git (workspace
   rule 3). Keys live in `~/.daemn/keys.env` on the owner's machine today;
   company-account keys land in the ruled key home when that migration runs.
6. The retired shared chain (`new-workflow-design/builds/video-teardown/`)
   is history, not a reference — this machine replaced it entirely
   (decision log 2026-08-25).

One check reports without stopping a run (the elements validation); the rest STOP it.

1. **The audit (stage 4e on the config, shown as 4f on the board).** Eleven
   checks of the finished script against the source. **Since 2026-09-30 a
   verdict other than SHIP holds the chain** (`AUDIT-HOLD.md`) — but what the
   swipe itself does is only ever a NOTE, never a FAIL (audit v8: "If the swipe
   has it, that's what we do"); each failed check
   is A<n>, passed only by a fix and re-run or `--approve-structure A5`. the owner:
   "do whatever is necessary to fix this problem" — a scene staging a result
   the product does not deliver had been reported by three passes and fixed by
   none.
2. **The elements validation** (`machine/elements_check.py`, 2026-09-20).
   After stage 1c files `doctrine.json`, every label in it — framework,
   awareness entry and exit, sophistication, sections, techniques, the
   delivery dials — is looked up in the shared element library
   (`components/elements/`) and written to `elements.json` beside it. A value
   the library does not hold is **recorded as unknown, never dropped and never
   nudged onto the nearest row**: it is the evidence that the library is
   missing a row. It costs nothing (two JSON reads) and never fails a run.
   The framework bank re-checks every banked run on refresh.
   Off: `VT_NO_ELEMENTS_CHECK=1`.
3. **The structure lock** (stage 3, 2026-09-24 — the one gate that STOPS the
   chain). the owner: "literally this cannot happen again UNLESS I DISCRETELY SAY
   SO. THE WHOLE POINT IS TO TAKE A SWIPE AND ADAPT, not ruin it."

The
   rewrite (v12) keeps every place, role, speaker and beat of the swipe; a
   brand's position files shape the words only. Any ELEMENT LEDGER row it
   marks Adapted or Dropped, and any STRUCTURE QUESTIONS FOR DAMON it raises,
   hold stage 3 (`status: held`, `STRUCTURE-CHECK.md` in the run) and nothing
   after it runs. Only the owner's numbers release it:
   `run.py <video> --approve-structure 2,Q1` (or `all`) re-checks the SAME
   rewrite — never re-writes it — and the prompt is told which changes he
   approved. There is no off switch. Test: `machine/test_structure_lock.py`.
4. **The swipe match** (stage 5, 2026-09-24 — STOPS the chain, and production
   refuses what it did not pass). the owner, before batching many videos for many
   brands: "make sure this never happens again, literally." The rewrite's
   own ledger is not trusted: `machine/swipe_match.py` has a judge (prompt
   `prompts/stage-5m-swipe-match/`, the strongest Gemini we hold) compare the
   FINISHED brief with the swipe's teardown shot by shot — place, people,
   camera, who speaks, order, added or dropped scenes — quoting the brief's
   own words, plus a machine check that a selfie shot stays a selfie. Every
   change is numbered M1, M2…; any not approved (`--approve-structure M2` or
   `all`) holds stage 5 and writes `SWIPE-MATCH.md`. The brief's first line
   carries the stamp; video-production's `run.py start` refuses a brief
   without `swipe-match: PASSED`, or one edited after its check (binding the
   cast is not an edit). `--composed` there is only for a brief made with no
   swipe. Findings

are kept per brief, so an approval never renumbers them.
   Test: `machine/test_swipe_match.py`.
5. **The manifest** (stage 5, right after the swipe match, 2026-09-24). the owner:
   "a manifest at the end of every brief to make sure teardown record, and
   final brief has the core elements that literally make this ad work before
   we can go into ai production — i do not have time to babysit this anymore."
   `machine/manifest.py` writes a block onto the END of the brief: every
   ELEMENT (E1…) and LOAD-BEARING item (L1…) of the replication spec pointed at
   the scene that carries it (a judge, prompt `prompts/stage-5n-manifest/`,
   quoting the brief), the swipe-match stamp, every person/look/voice/place/
   product/prop banked or to make, and every $ figure found in `brands/<brand>/`
   or flagged. Last line `MANIFEST: COMPLETE` or `MISSING — …`, tied to the
   brief's fingerprint. A missing core element or unsourced price holds stage
   5; elements still to make do not (that is a fresh brief's normal state).
   video-production re-checks it before spending and refuses anything but
   COMPLETE. A missing core element passes only on `--approve-structure E6`.

6. **Every line of the swipe** (stages 1 and 3, 2026-09-24). The teardown
   model was asked for the transcript "word for word" and wrote 9 fragments
   for 26 spoken lines ("…" for the rest, two lines in the wrong mouth), and
   every later stage lost the swipe's back-and-forth. Now `machine/transcript.py`
   runs right after stage 1: the audio is transcribed (ElevenLabs speech-to-text,
   speakers separated), one

numbered line per speaker turn (T1…), appended to
   the teardown record as `### VERBATIM TRANSCRIPT` and kept as
   `transcript.json`. The spec (v4) lists a real exchange as an element; the
   injection (v13) carries one row per T-number; the stage-3 gate holds any
   missing number as a Dropped change.

7. **The hook is a format** (stage 4b, 2026-09-25 — STOPS the chain). the owner:
   "we're building out a format … all we want to do is adjust its variables …
   we just inject words from our language bank." Then: "this is literally
   perfect. This is how we get this done." Hooks prompt v16 prints the source's
   opening line, card and first frame with named `[BLANKS]`; every blank is a
   named ELEMENT with what it must hold, in element names only
   (`[PLACE] holds [EXPERT]`). The control fills the blanks with the swap;
   each variation keeps every fixed word and fills the blanks from the
   avatar's own words; `[RESEARCH: …]` blanks are researched with a receipt.
   `machine/hook_format.py` checks, with no model: the format's words are the
   source's own (line and card), no blank swallowed a shared word (repaired
   mechanically when it did), every version keeps every fixed word, every
   blank has an ELEMENTS line. A break holds 4b (`HOOK-FORMAT.md`);
   `--approve-structure H3` passes one. Creativity is the spice's job, not
   the hooks'. Test: `machine/test_hook_format.py`.

8. **The route lock** (every writing stage, 2026-09-30 — STOPS the chain at
   the end of the teardown). the owner's four stations (2026-09-25): tearing a
   swipe down is one job and writing

our version is another, and writing
   starts only on a route a person picked — creator, ai or founder
   (`--route`). There is no default any more, and 1b's ROUTE RECOMMENDED is
   printed as a suggestion and never switches the run ("it kept going and
   wrote for the wrong thing"). With no route, stages 0, 1, 1k, 1c and 2 run,
   every other stage waits, `run.json` carries `waiting_for: route`, and the
   run is filed like any teardown. A run already written on a route before
   the lock keeps it. Map and hand-offs: `notes/four-stations-map-damon.md`,
   `notes/four-stations-contracts-damon.md`. Test: `machine/test_route_lock.py`.

9. **No more frames** (2026-09-30, the owner: "no more frames, only the brief and
   swipe file link"). Stage 6 never runs, on any route. Every brief opens with
   `**Swipe file:** <link>` (creator brief v28, AI brief v19, her page v7), and
   the creator and founder brief end each concept with HOW TO SAY IT — the
   spice sheet turned into notes she reads. Test: `machine/test_route_lock.py`.

10. **Every person is the swipe's person, and the brief says so** (stage 5,
   2026-10-01 — STOPS the chain). the owner: "why did you make doctor 3 a woman
   if you knew it was a man?" then "did the brief follow the element?"
   `machine/cast_match.py` pairs each brief person with the swipe person they
   stand in for and compares gender (P-), then reads every word of the brief
   about that person — the readable cast block (R-) and every scene direction
   (D-, their own hands, clothes and look) — against their banked element.
   Any finding holds stage

5; `cast_match.repair()` fixes the words from the
   element. Production's element check (3.1) runs the same reading.
   Test: `machine/test_cast_match.py`. Then, on an AI brief, **production's own
   brief contract** (video-production `model_inputs.brief_violations`) — anything
   production would refuse holds the brief here, not at the spend (2026-10-01).

11. **The swipe, shot by shot** (stage 1 + stage 5, 2026-10-01 — STOPS the
   chain at 5). the owner: "map out every single frame so when we describe what
   happens in our version it's as close as possible to the swipe." After the
   transcript, `machine/framemap.py` finds every cut in the pixels and has the
   strongest Gemini watch each shot at 8 fps (prompt
   `prompts/stage-1f-frame-map/`): who is in frame, start and end frame, camera,
   every moment with its time and body geometry, words on screen, sound, edit,
   and the capture (resolution, fps, bitrate). `framemap/FRAME-MAP.md` feeds
   the brief as `{frame_map}`. At stage 5 the brief is held on any swipe insert
   it has no scene for, any on-screen word it drops, or an arm entering from
   another edge (video-production `storyboard_plan.swipe_carry`, F<n>;
   `--approve-structure F3` passes one). Tests: `machine/test_framemap.py`,
   video-production `machine/test_storyboard_plan.py`.

12. **The swipe's style and format** (stage 0, 2026-10-09). the owner, after a
   3D-animated swipe came back as a photoreal cast (and the doll ads before
   it): "we need to also know the actual creative style and format that it's
   in … it needs to be picked up so we're not

wasting time on credits." Triage
   v3 names both as element-library ids (`{styles}`, `{formats}`, the
   brand-free lists) or `new:<name>`; `run.py` writes `style_id` and
   `format_id` onto `run.json`, which the shelves copy into the repo with
   every swipe. Production's element makers put that style at the top of
   every prompt in place of photoreal and refuse a style the bank does not
   hold (video-production `make_character.style_lock`). Tests:
   `machine/test_swipe_style.py`, video-production
   `machine/test_swipe_style_lock.py`. Chain doc: video-production
   `THE-CHAIN.md`, "The swipe's style is read at 1".

Also at the end of every run (2026-09-20): the run's words are **copied** to
the repo's one home for run records, on two shelves with one slug
(2026-09-30, the owner: "naming needs to be lined up cleanly across all the
tools"): `runs/video-teardown/<brand>/<slug>/` holds what was read off the
swipe (stages 0, 1, 1k, 1c, 2, the transcript, the Sound Sheet, `doctrine.json`,
`elements.json`, `post-talk.json`) and `runs/video-writing/<brand>/<slug>/` holds everything
written for the brand (1b, 3, 4a–4g, 5, 7, 7b, 8, RULINGS, swipe match,
manifest, `deliverable/` — the brief production takes). `run.json` sits on
both. `machine/file_run.py`; text only, nothing over 1 MB. Test:
`machine/test_shelves.py`. Every filing also rebuilds the brief index,
`runs/video-writing/INDEX.md` + `index.json` (`machine/brief_index.py`, test
`machine/test_brief_index.py`) — one row per brief, joined to its production
runs by their `brief_from` and to edits by the kit's `from_run`.

`machine/runs/<slug>/` is still the working folder and nothing moved.
Off: `VT_NO_REPO_FILING=1`.

items.section: How to run a teardown — one way
items.text:
You work inside **Higgsfield Supercomputer** with this repo cloned into it.
(Claude Code with the repo cloned works the same way.) You do not paste files
into a chat, you do not copy anything into a Drive, you do not install
anything. You say what you want and it runs the chain.

---

items.doc: How to run a teardown — one way
items.text:

Say: **"Copy brands/_TEMPLATE to brands/<my brand> and walk me through
filling it in."** It asks you the questions in the template's README, in
order, and writes your answers into the files. Every tool reads this folder,
so you explain your brand once.

product the way a camera sees it — the container, the colour, the finish,

items.text:
Say: **"Tear down this video for <my brand>"** and give it the video — a

   ear, its visual style and its format — a 3D-animated piece stays

can make the video without asking you a single question, it worked. If they
have to interpret anything, go back and make that part specific.

**Two lines, and the one thing they share.**

 

Reading a swiped video is one job. What you do with it is two.

Tearing a source down — what is on screen, who it is for, the reusable machine
underneath — does not care who performs the result. Everything after that does,
and the two jobs have almost nothing in common: one ends with a person holding
a phone in their own bathroom, the other with nobody on set at all.

 

**The front half stays shared on purpose.** Two teardowns of the same source
would drift, and then the two lines would be arguing about what the video
actually was.

Creator — AI.

Production instruction — what to film, with what they own — CUT owned footage, GENERATE, or COMPOSITE.

both". Until then it was one chain with a `--route` flag, and the flag was a

A swiped video goes in. A shot-ready creator brief comes out — script, hooks,
wardrobe, and a picture on every scene.

   said, the wardrobe.
2. **Makes it ours.** Substitutes our brand into the format that already
   works, without changing anything that's *worn* or *revealed on camera* —
   only what's held up or referred to.
3. **Runs the DR loop.** Writes the opening hooks straight off the source,
   then decides where our product enters, then (if the source needs it)
   builds out the middle, then closes it, then checks the whole thing
   against the source and the rules.

   on every scene, a picture for every scene. Nothing the maker doesn't need.

items.section: The one decision that changes everything: the lane
items.text:
The very first stage (**Triage**) looks at the source and calls one of four
lanes. Everything downstream reads that call:

Lane — What it means — What changes.
**ALREADY AN AD** — The source already has a hook, a proof beat, an offer — **Expansion is skipped.** Nothing gets added — a proof run added zero beats to an ad and it still worked. The close builds straight off the injection..
**ORGANIC** — No pitch anywhere in the source — **Full chain runs.** Nothing commercial exists yet — the hooks, the placement, the expansion, all of it gets built from nothing..
**STATIC / SEQUENTIAL** — Not a video — a still or a carousel — This chain stops. Belongs in the image lane instead..

items.section: The tracker is the list, not a copy of it (2026-08-27)
items.text:
`tracker.py` reads the brand's own creator sheet through the service account.
`--check` says what the sheet has that the machine doesn't and the other way
round; `--sync` rewrites `creators.json` from it. The sheet id lives in
`brands/<brand>/tracker.json`, never here.

This exists because a hand-typed copy silently went stale: a signed partner sat
on the sheet marked *waiting for brief* and the machine had never heard of her,
and two more appeared during a single afternoon. Run `--check` before a pull;
a row that contradicts itself gets said out loud rather than quietly doing
nothing.

Any list of creators or posts is sorted by view count, biggest first, before
anything else is applied. Fit, usability and how many videos someone still
owes are filters laid over that order — never a reordering. Reach is the thing
being bought; a list re-sorted on someone's judgement hides it.

items.section: What counts as a source (the owner, 2026-08-27)
items.text:
Only **video ads** get torn down: the creator performing, on screen. A quote
card over stock footage, a still, a carousel, or b-roll whose whole content is
the caption over it is not a source, no matter how well it scored.

Triage will not stop these — its STATIC / SEQUENTIAL lane tests the *file*, so
anything that arrives as a real mp4 with motion and sound passes as ORGANIC
and the full chain runs. And the sourcing rank will not stop them either: that
is `views + likes + comments` with no eyes on it. **The check happens before
the run, by whoever picks the post — look at the thumbnail.** A quote card
ranked first on a creator's page on 2026-08-26 and took thirteen stages to
produce a brief with nobody in it.

A second decision happens after placement: it asks not just *"where does our
product go"* but *"where does the viewer cross into recognising their own
problem"* — because on organic sources, that crossing is usually a **problem
named on screen**, with no product in frame yet, not a product shot. Only if
neither exists at all does a brief become a *hook asset* (an opening that
earns a click and hands off, never asked to sell).

items.doc: Which models to use, and the settings that work
items.text:
When you upload a swipe video and ask it to describe every scene, that is a
Gemini model doing the watching.

Use — Model.
First choice — `gemini-3-flash-preview`.
If it is busy — `gemini-3.5-flash`.
For a long or complicated video — `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.
Flash is the right default — it is fast and it does not miss scenes. Only
reach for Pro when a video is long, dense, or full of overlapping dialogue.

items.doc: Which models to use, and the settings that work
items.text:
Every still starts here: `text2image_soul_v2`.

Setting — Value — Why.
Size — 1536 × 2048 — portrait, enough resolution to crop.
Style — General — anything else fights your prompt.
`enhance_prompt` — **off** — on, it rewrites you and drifts off the brief.
Seed — fixed, one per character — the same number gives you the same face.
**The character-sheet trick.** Before you generate any scene, make one image
per person as a split-screen sheet: full body on the left, chest-up close-up
on the right, both the same character. Then feed that sheet in as the
reference for every scene they appear in. That is what stops them being a
different human in every shot — it is the single biggest difference between
work that looks made and work that looks broken.

---

items.doc: Which models to use, and the settings that work
items.text:
Frames become video with `seedance_2_0`.

Setting — Value.
Ratio / size — 9:16, 1080 × 1920.
`mode` — `std`.
`generate_audio` — `true` — it invents its own ambience and dialogue.
`multi_shots` — `false` — one shot per generation, always.
`speedramp` — `auto`.
Length — **4s per scene beat**, 6s for silent b-roll.
Longer single takes (8–15s) work when one continuous moment carries the beat,
but cutting 4-second shots is what holds attention.

Feed each generation the character sheet plus a full cinematic description of
the moment — not a shot label. "Cinematic drama, golden morning market stall.
The elderly woman from the reference image reaches across the counter…" beats
"scene 3, woman at stall" every time.

items.doc: Which models to use, and the settings that work
items.section: Voice, if you need it — Seed Audio
items.text:
`seed_audio`, wav, 24000 Hz.

Setting — Value.
`speech_rate` — −5 to −15 (slower reads as more serious).
`loudness_rate` · `pitch_rate` — 0.
`expression_intensity` — 5.
No voice presets. Describe the person in words, and clone from an uploaded
reference file when you want a specific voice.

Note: if Seedance is already generating audio for a shot, you do not need a
separate voice track for it. Use Seed Audio for narration over the cut.

items.section: The order you do it in
items.text:
1. Character sheets — one per person, fixed seed. **Do this first, always.**
2. Frames — the brief's image prompt plus the character sheet as reference.
3. Shots — Seedance, 4 seconds, one shot per generation.
4. Voice — only if the cut needs narration.

items.text:
**A different face every shot** — you skipped the character sheet, or changed
the seed. Go back to step 1.

**It ignored half your prompt** — `enhance_prompt` is on. Turn it off.

**Everything feels stiff** — your prompts are shot labels, not descriptions.
Write what a person watching would see.

**The product looks wrong** — nothing in the prompt told it what the product
looks like. That comes from your brand folder; fill that part in.
